en: The Mental Worship of Śrī Śiva according to the Heart's Devotion (Śrī Śivamānasapūjā)
A seat fashioned of jewels, a bath with Himalayan waters, divine garments adorned with various gems, sandalwood marked with the fragrance of musk,
flowers made of jasmine, campaka, and bilva leaves, and likewise incense.
O Lord, O ocean of compassion, O Pashupati, please accept this lamp offered within my heart. ||1||
In a golden vessel inlaid with pieces of the nine gems, there was ghee, milk-rice, five kinds of solid foods, along with milk, curd, plantains, and syrups;
and ten thousand varieties of vegetables, water made delicious by pieces of camphor, and fragrant substances.
O Lord, please accept this betel-roll mentally prepared by me with devotion. ||2||
The parasol, a pair of chowries, a fan, a stainless mirror,
the arts of the lute, the kettledrum, the clay drum, and the trumpet, as well as song and dance,
prostration with the eight limbs, and manifold hymns— all this has indeed been performed by me.
O All-pervading Lord, O Master, accept this worship offered by my resolve. ||3||
You are the Self; the daughter of the mountain is your intellect; your companions are the vital breaths; the body is your home;
the arrangement for the enjoyment of sense objects is your worship; sleep is your state of meditative absorption (samādhi);
the movement of your feet is the rite of circumambulation; and all your words are hymns of praise.
Whatever action I perform, O Śambhu, all of it is for your worship. ||4||
Thus, whoever should daily remember these four verses of service during the worship of Hara at the three junctions of the day, their daily worship of Hari becomes mental;
such a person shall attain happiness and the direct vision of the radiant Lord Hari himself.
Having taken that garment at the time of her great departure, she went to the world of Kailāsa.
Whether it be an offense committed by hand or foot, born of speech or body, produced by action, or arising from the ears, eyes, or mind.
Whether known or unknown, forgive all of this;
victory, victory to you, O ocean of compassion, Śrī Mahādeva Śambhu!
